svg.aria-label: What Beamtime adds to experiment tracking for simulations, training runs and other numerical experiments: testable hypotheses, people and agents working on one shared record, notes and memory written together, views built from reusable blocks, plain files you own, and cluster runs seen over ssh; with the research cycle: theory, literature, ideas and questions feed a proposal, then experiments, check, verdict and memory.
svg.title: What Beamtime adds
svg.text: What Beamtime adds
Experiment tracking for simulations, training runs and any numerical experiment, made for people and agents working together.
FEATURE
USUALLY
WITH BEAMTIME
Testable hypotheses

text.tspan: say what you expect, then check it

svg.text: Hypotheses live in your head, a doc, or buried
in your coding agent's chat history.
Proposals, the experiments that test them, notes and
verdicts in one place; predictions are checked for you.
People and agents, together

text.tspan: one shared record of every experiment

svg.text: Runs sit on a hosted server; agents reach
them through a remote API.
Agents work on the run files themselves, local or remote,
with fast, compact MCP answers. Everything in one place.
Notes and memory, written together

text.tspan: by people and agents, shown in the UI

svg.text: Notes and reports drift apart from the runs
and from what was predicted.
Notes record verdicts next to the data; a shared memory
keeps the big picture. All of it visible in the UI.
Views you fully control

text.tspan: reusable blocks; coding is not the bottleneck

svg.text: Dashboards clicked together for each project,
hard to reuse or hand to an agent.
Agents build any view you ask for from reusable blocks;
a good view, once made, serves every new experiment.
Plain files you own

text.tspan: no server, no database, no account

svg.text: Data locked in a hosted service, a database
or binary event files.
Every run is a plain folder you can read, search and
version. Nothing to host, nothing to migrate.
Built for clusters
Jobs need network to upload, or offline runs
are synced by hand later.
See your cluster runs from your laptop over ssh: only the
answers travel, and compute nodes need no internet.
